units.locator: Article 32.13. Enforcement of a ruling imposing compulsory work
units.text: 7. Women with children under three years of age and (or) children with disabilities, or who are adoptive parents, guardians or custodians of such children, and men who are single parents with children under three years of age and (or) children with disabilities, or who are the sole adoptive parents, guardians or custodians of such children, who have been subjected to the administrative penalty of compulsory work, as well as a person subjected to that penalty who is recognised as having a group I or II disability, becomes pregnant or develops a serious illness preventing service of compulsory work, have the right to apply to a court for release from further service of compulsory work. A bailiff also has the right to submit such an application to the court in respect of the persons listed. If the application is granted, the judge shall issue a ruling terminating enforcement of the ruling imposing the administrative penalty of compulsory work.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 32.13

units.locator: Article 32.13. Enforcement of a ruling imposing compulsory work
units.text: 8. A person subjected to the administrative penalty of compulsory work shall perform that work without remuneration.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 32.13

units.locator: Article 32.13. Enforcement of a ruling imposing compulsory work
units.text: 9. The period of compulsory work shall be calculated in the hours during which the person subjected to that administrative penalty actually served compulsory work.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 32.13

units.locator: Article 32.13. Enforcement of a ruling imposing compulsory work
units.text: 10. Compulsory work may not exceed four hours on days off and on days when the person subjected to the administrative penalty of compulsory work is not engaged in their principal work, service or studies, or two hours after work, service or studies on working days. Upon a written application by the person subjected to that administrative penalty, the bailiff may increase the maximum compulsory work time to eight hours on days off and on days when the person is not engaged in their principal work, service or studies, and to four hours after work, service or studies on working days. As a rule, compulsory work may not amount to less than twelve hours per week. Where there are valid reasons, the bailiff may permit the person subjected to the administrative penalty of compulsory work to work fewer hours during a week.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 32.13

units.locator: Article 32.13. Enforcement of a ruling imposing compulsory work
units.text: 11. The management of the organisation in which a person subjected to the administrative penalty of compulsory work serves that work shall be responsible for monitoring performance of the work assigned to the person and notifying the bailiff of the number of hours worked or the person’s evasion of compulsory work.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 32.13

units.locator: Article 32.13. Enforcement of a ruling imposing compulsory work
units.text: 12. If a person subjected to the administrative penalty of compulsory work evades serving it through repeated refusal to perform work, and (or) repeated failure to report for compulsory work without valid reasons, and (or) repeated breaches of labour discipline, as confirmed by documents of the organisation in which the person serves compulsory work, the bailiff shall draw up an administrative offence record under part 4 of Article 20.25 of this Code.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 32.13

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.label: Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.label: Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: 1. A ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held must be complied with by the person held administratively liable.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: 2. The federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall maintain a list of persons subjected to the type of administrative penalty specified in part 1 of this article, to ensure enforcement of rulings imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held (hereinafter, the list of persons).
units.label: Part 2 Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: 3. The federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall enter information in the list of persons no later than three working days from the day it receives a copy of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held that has entered into force.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: 4. A person shall be deemed removed from the list of persons upon expiry of the administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held, or when the federal executive body responsible for internal affairs has received a judicial act that has entered into force quashing the ruling imposing that administrative ban.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: 5. The federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall remove information from the list of persons no later than three working days following the day the administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held expires, or no later than three working days from the day it receives a copy of a judicial act that has entered into force quashing the ruling imposing that administrative ban.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: 6. The information contained in the list of persons (the surname, given name, patronymic (if any), date and place of birth of the person in respect of whom the court’s decision imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held has entered into legal force; the date and number of that court decision; and the dates on which the administrative penalty begins and expires) shall be open to public inspection.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 32.14

units.locator: Article 32.14. Enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
units.text: 7. Access to the information contained in the list of persons shall be provided through the official website of the federal executive body responsible for internal affairs on the Internet information and telecommunications network. No charge shall be made for access to the information contained in the list of persons published by that body on its official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 32.14
